reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that displacement covariances improve vibrational entropy estimates for elemental solids, but it does not address liquids, high-entropy alloys, or the construction of corrected potentials for thermodynamic integration. The key premises about transferability to liquid HEAs and the specific error reduction target are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Displacement covariance matrices from AIMD can capture many-body vibrational correlations in solids.
These covariance-based corrections can be incorporated into a potential to improve phase-space overlap.
The approach is transferable from elemental solids to high-entropy alloy liquids near melting.
A Gaussian approximation for atomic displacements is sufficient to represent anharmonic liquid configurations.
The correction will reduce thermodynamic integration mismatch to below ~5 meV/atom.
